step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 24-year-old pregnant woman (mother) and her female neonate with congenital syphilis and necrotizing funisitis

evidence_items.source_quote: Following cesarean section, the mother was diagnosed with syphilis by a serological test.

Congenital syphilis was confirmed by serology of the neonate: rapid plasma region 32x, Treponema pallidum hemagglutination 1280x, and a positive immunoglobulin fluorescent treponemal antibody-absorption test.
Numerous T. pallidum were detected by IHC, which uses an antibody against T. pallidum (Figure 1).

rationale: 24-year-old woman delivered a neonate with congenital syphilis and necrotizing funisitis. Mother was serologically diagnosed with syphilis, neonate had RPR 32x, TPHA 1280x, and FTA-ABS+, and placental/cord IHC detected numerous T. pallidum (E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 62-year-old female with neurosyphilis mimicking anti-LGI1 limbic encephalitis

evidence_items.source_quote: The serum testing of routine blood tests, coagulation profile, liver function and kidney function tests, blood sugars, lipid profile, and serological testing for hepatitis B, syphilis, and HIV were negative.
The patient had a positive RPR with a serum titer of 1:16 and a positive TPPA. Subsequently, TPPA and RPR in CSF were tested, and both results were positive.
The patient received intravenous penicillin sodium 3.5 million units every 4 h for 14 days to treat the NS.

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial routine syphilis screening was reported negative, but subsequent quantitative serum RPR (1:16), serum TPPA, CSF RPR, and CSF TPPA were all positive.
rationale: 62-year-old woman presenting with limbic encephalitis-like seizures and anti-LGI1 antibodies. Despite an initial negative screen, repeat testing showed positive serum RPR (1:16), serum TPPA, CSF RPR, and CSF TPPA (E1 confirmatory for neurosyphilis), with resolution on IV penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 65-year-old Caucasian male with syphilitic optic neuropathy/neurosyphilis and secondary autoimmune optic neuropathy

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum treponemal antibodies and Treponema pallidum particle agglutination were reactive, with rapid plasma reagin reactive titre of 1,280.
evidence_items.test_name: Serum treponemal Ab, TPPA, and RPR

evidence_items.source_quote: Lumbar puncture showed CSF weakly reactive to T. pallidum antibodies (EIA, fluorescent) and T. pallidum particle agglutination.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF T. pallidum EIA and TPPA

rationale: 65-year-old male with bilateral optic neuropathy, tonic pupils, and history of primary chancre 12 months prior. Serum RPR was 1:1280 with reactive treponemal antibodies and TPPA, plus CSF reactive to T. pallidum EIA/TPPA (E2 highly specific). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 55-year-old male with acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis and neurosyphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: Finally, we had access to the serologic tests results that revealed a positive VDRL (1/128) and FTA-ABS.
A lumbar puncture revealed a positive VDRL and CSF-TPHA in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
Follow-up serologic testing revealed a decrease of VDRL to 1/32.

rationale: 55-year-old male with acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis. Serum VDRL (1:128) and FTA-ABS were positive, CSF VDRL and CSF-TPHA were positive (E1 confirmatory), and VDRL decreased 4-fold to 1:32 after IV penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 37-year-old male with secondary syphilitic hepatitis/cholestasis

evidence_items.source_quote: RPR returned positive with a reflex titer of 1:64. Treponema pallidum IgG was sent for confirmation and it was reactive.
evidence_items.test_name: Serum RPR and T. pallidum IgG

evidence_items.source_quote: Warthin starry stain was negative. Immunochemical stain for Treponema pallidum revealed no organisms.
evidence_items.test_name: Liver biopsy Warthin-Starry and T. pallidum IHC

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was given a single dose treatment: penicillin G 2.4 million units intramuscular route (IM) once. He showed symptomatic improvement subsequently, including resolution of nausea/RUQ abdominal pain.

step10_contradiction_notes: Liver biopsy Warthin-Starry and T. pallidum IHC stains were negative, but high-titer RPR (1:64), reactive T. pallidum IgG, cholestatic hepatitis, and rapid response to benzathine penicillin G establish syphilitic hepatitis.
rationale: 37-year-old male presenting with cholestatic hepatitis. RPR was positive at 1:64 with reactive T. pallidum IgG (E2), and symptoms and LFTs rapidly improved after IM penicillin G despite negative liver tissue stains. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 43-year-old HIV+ male with secondary syphilis causing hepatitis and pancreatitis

evidence_items.source_quote: He had a macular, darkly pigmented rash on the palms and soles, as well as bilateral nontender inguinal lymphadenopathy (Figure 3).
An RPR was ordered and returned weakly positive at 1 : 8 and a T. pallidum antibody test returned positive.
Treatment was initiated with intramuscular benzathine penicillin G (2.4 million units) given weekly for three weeks. Over the next two weeks liver and pancreatic enzyme levels declined.

rationale: 43-year-old HIV+ male with palmar/plantar macular rash, nontender inguinal lymphadenopathy, RPR 1:8, and positive T. pallidum antibody test (E2), with normalization of hepatic and pancreatic enzymes after benzathine penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 48-year-old male with HIV, primary/neurosyphilis, papillitis, and SIADH

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests revealed a reactive Rapid Plasma Reagin (RPR)-titer of 1:32, a T. pallidum haemagglutination assay (TPHA) titer of 1:2560 and positive T. pallidum IgM and IgG immunoblots (recomBlot, Mikrogen, Germany).
evidence_items.test_name: RPR, TPHA, and T. pallidum IgM/IgG immunoblot

evidence_items.source_quote: The RT-PCR detected the presence of T. pallidum DNA in the swabs from oral and genital lesions, but not from the anal swab.

The T. pallidum IgG immunoblot from the cerebrospinal fluid was also positive showing the presence of additional and higher-intensity bands compared to the serum sample. This indicated intrathecal antibody production and suggested neurosyphilis.

rationale: 48-year-old HIV+ male with primary oral/genital ulcers, unilateral papillitis, and hyponatremia/SIADH. T. pallidum DNA was detected by RT-PCR in oral and genital swabs (E1 confirmatory), with RPR 1:32, TPHA 1:2560, and positive CSF IgG immunoblot. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 55-year-old male with syphilitic aortic aneurysm and lung adenocarcinoma

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood tests revealed positive results of treponemalpallidum particle agglutination (TPHA) and fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption test (FTA-Abs) and HIV test was negative.
Cardiac ultrasound revealed ectasia of aorta ascendens. So the computed tomography angiography (CTA) and 3dimensional (3D) reconstructions of cardiac vessels were performed (Fig. 1).
evidence_items.test_name: Cardiac ultrasound and CTA ascending aorta

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on the symptoms, blood results and the CT images, diagnosis is confirmed as syphilitic aortic aneurysm.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical diagnosis of syphilitic aortic aneurysm

rationale: 55-year-old male with syphilitic ascending aortic aneurysm (ectasia on cardiac US and CTA) and positive TPHA and FTA-Abs (E2 tertiary syphilis criteria), treated with IV ceftriaxone and endovascular intervention. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 54-year-old male with monkeypox and secondary syphilis coinfection

evidence_items.source_quote: However, 6 days after the initiation of tecovirimat treatment, he started noticing a new rash all over his body, including the trunk, arms, legs, palms, and soles.
evidence_items.test_name: Diffuse rash on palms and soles

evidence_items.source_quote: The serum rapid plasma reagin (RPR) titer was very high at 1:16384, confirming the diagnosis of secondary syphilis. The patient was treated with 2.4 million units of intramuscular benzathine penicillin.
His serum RPR titer responded very well with drop to 1:256 over a period of 2 months.

rationale: 54-year-old male with monkeypox coinfected with secondary syphilis. Developed a diffuse rash involving palms and soles with serum RPR titer of 1:16384 (E2) and rapid clinical and serological response (64-fold RPR drop to 1:256) after benzathine penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 38-year-old mother with latent syphilis and male neonate with congenital syphilis (metadata age=38, gender=Male mixes mother and neonate)

evidence_items.source_quote: Her rapid plasma reagin (RPR) test was reactive in 1:2 dilution. The confirmatory treponema pallidum hemagglutination (TPHA) test was also positive.

However, RPR was reactive in 1:64 dilution, and TPHA was positive. Maternal RPR at the time of delivery was nonreactive. The child was diagnosed as a case of congenital syphilis and admitted in the neonatal intensive care unit.
evidence_items.test_name: Neonate RPR 1:64 and TPHA (>=4-fold higher than maternal delivery RPR)

rationale: 38-year-old mother treated for latent syphilis (RPR 1:2, TPHA+) delivered a male neonate with congenital syphilis (RPR 1:64, TPHA+, >4-fold higher than maternal delivery RPR of nonreactive; E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 36-year-old HIV+ male with secondary syphilis osteitis

evidence_items.source_quote: Evaluation for additional sexually transmitted infections revealed a negative acute hepatitis panel but a positive rapid plasma reagin (RPR) with a titer of 1 : 64. Confirmatory testing with Treponema pallidum antibody (TP-PA) testing was positive.
Because of the concern for syphilis, a modified Steiner stain was performed which demonstrated several spirochetes within the epidermis.
Prior to discharge (hospital course, day 8), a repeat RPR was performed, with a declining titer of 1 : 32.

rationale: 36-year-old HIV+ male with secondary syphilis osteitis. Modified Steiner silver stain demonstrated spirochetes in the epidermis (E1 confirmatory), RPR was 1:64 with positive TP-PA, and lesions/bone pain resolved on doxycycline. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 54-year-old man with neurosyphilis, Argyll Robertson pupil, and seizures

evidence_items.source_quote: All the cranial nerves were normal on examination except the Argyll Robertson pupil which showed no reaction to the light (Supplementary Video 1).

Serologic tests and CSF analysis were both positive for syphilis and so were the serum rapid plasma regain (titer 1:2) and treponema pallidum particle agglutination (TPPA) assay. The serum toludine red unheated serum test (TRUST) titer was 1:2. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) TPPA and fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption (TA-Abs) analysis unveiled similar indication.

rationale: 54-year-old man with neurosyphilis presenting with seizures and Argyll Robertson pupil (E2), positive serum RPR (1:2), TRUST (1:2), TPPA, and CSF TPPA/FTA-Abs with CSF pleocytosis, responsive to IV penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 46-year-old male with secondary pulmonary syphilis and syphilitic nephrotic syndrome

evidence_items.source_quote: His serology was negative for  HIV and hepatitis B, but positive for T. pallidum antibody (TPAb).
In the interim, the result of RPR came back positive with a titre of 1:256

AE1/3 highlighted entrapped reactive alveolar  structures and T. pallidum antibody was positive. The granulomatous inflammation and positive TPAb supported a final diagnosis of pulmonary syphilis with early necrotic granulomas being precursors of gummas.

rationale: 46-year-old male with pulmonary pseudo-tumor and nephrotic syndrome. Lung biopsy T. pallidum immunohistochemistry was positive (E1 confirmatory), serum RPR was 1:256 with positive TPAb, and lung mass and proteinuria resolved with RPR dropping to 1:64 after benzylpenicillin. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 25-year-old Qatari male with secondary syphilis and reversible otosyphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on this typical skin rash, a diagnosis of secondary syphilis was suspected, and serum treponemal as well as non-treponemal tests were ordered, which came back positive with RPR titer 1:32.
A follow-up serum RPR showed a significant titer reduction (repeat RPR 1:4).

rationale: 25-year-old male with prior painless penile ulcer, diffuse non-itchy palmoplantar maculopapular rash, positive treponemal and RPR (1:32) serology (E2 secondary syphilis syndrome), subsequent otosyphilis with sensorineural hearing loss resolving after 14 days of IV penicillin G, and 8-fold RPR titer drop to 1:4. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 15-year-old female with secondary syphilis (facial elegant syphilides, tongue mucous plaques, palmar syphilitic roseola).

evidence_items.source_quote: The clinical diagnosis was secondary syphilis, confirmed using quantitative VDRL (1/32) and rapid treponemal test (FTA-ABS) reagents.

rationale: 15-year-old female with facial syphilides, tongue mucous plaques, and palmar syphilitic roseola with Biett collarette, confirmed by high-titer VDRL (1:32) and positive FTA-ABS, resolving with benzathine penicillin. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 36-year-old African American HIV-positive man with rupioid secondary syphilis (IRIS).

evidence_items.source_quote: The fluorescent treponemal antibody (FTA-ABS) was positive, and the rapid plasma reagin titer was very highly reactive at 1:1,024.
Acid-fast bacilli (AFB), cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses, and Warthin-Starry staining were negative.

step10_contradiction_notes: Warthin-Starry silver stain on skin biopsy was negative, and patient had a remote history of treated syphilis; however, very high RPR titer (1:1,024), positive FTA-ABS, rupioid lesions, Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, and complete resolution with IV penicillin G confirm active rupioid secondary syphilis.
rationale: 36-year-old HIV-positive man initially misdiagnosed with peripheral T-cell lymphoma who presented with rupioid crusted plaques after restarting ART. FTA-ABS was positive and RPR was 1:1,024 (E2 high-titer secondary syphilis), with rapid resolution on IV penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 49-year-old female with isolated oral secondary syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests for syphilis showed a positive venereal diseases research laboratory (VDRL) at a titer of 1/32 and a reactive T. pallidum hemagglutination test. Based on these data, a diagnosis of secondary syphilis was made.

rationale: 49-year-old woman with isolated whitish-gray mucous plaques on the tongue, plasma-cell dermal infiltrate on biopsy, high-titer VDRL (1:32), and reactive TPHA (E2 secondary syphilis syndrome), resolving completely 15 days after benzathine penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 42-year-old heterosexual male with primary syphilitic balanitis of Follmann.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient then received the blood tests for STDs, including Treponema pallidum particle agglutination assay (TPPA), Rapid plasma reagin (RPR) assay, and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV); Herpes simplex virus (HSV) type 1IgG, IgM, HSV type 2 IgG, IgM, which revealed positive in TPPA and HSV1, 2IgG test, and negative in RPR, HIV, HSV1, and 2 IgM tests.

Sixty days after treatment, the patient came back to the hospital again for the follow-up of the serum treponema and non-treponemal tests, which showed positive TPPA and RPR, and the RPR titer was 1:1.

rationale: 42-year-old man with infiltrative hard erythematous coronal sulcus balanitis 3 weeks after unprotected sex (prior syphilis screen negative 15 months prior). Admission TPPA was positive with negative RPR, followed by documented RPR seroconversion to 1:1 at 60 days alongside TPPA positivity (E1 documented seroconversion + dual reactivity) and rapid healing after benzathine penicillin. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 5-month-old male infant with delayed diagnosis of congenital syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Subsequently, the infant had a negative serum Venereal Diseases Research Laboratory (VDRL) test but a positive treponemal antibodies (by Treponema pallidum indirect hemagglutination assay-TPHA).

The rapid plasma reagin test (RPR) was positive at a dilution of 1:256, and the TPHA also was reactive at 1:20480, both of which were 4-fold higher than the respective maternal titers (RPR 1:32; TPHA 1:2560).
evidence_items.test_name: Infant vs maternal RPR and TPHA titers

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial serum VDRL was negative despite positive TPHA, likely due to prozone or lab variation; repeat RPR (1:256) and TPHA (1:20480) were 4-fold higher than maternal titers (RPR 1:32, TPHA 1:2560) alongside snuffles, rash, failure to thrive, and periostitis.
rationale: 5-month-old male infant with congenital syphilis presenting with salmon-colored rash, snuffles, failure to thrive, and long-bone periostitis. Infant RPR (1:256) and TPHA (1:20480) were 4-fold higher than maternal titers (E1 confirmatory), treated with 10 days IV aqueous penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 40-year-old man with partially treated secondary syphilis ('acral pebbles').

evidence_items.source_quote: Venereal disease research laboratory test (VDRL) was positive in 1:4 dilution.
Warthin starry stain did not demonstrate the organisms.
Treponema pallidum hemagglutination (TPHA) test was positive in the titers of 1:1200.

step10_contradiction_notes: Warthin-Starry stain on finger biopsy was negative and VDRL was 1:4 after partial prior treatment; resolved by TPHA 1:1200, partially healed painless penile chancre, palmar papules with positive Buschke-Ollendorff sign, plasma-cell histopathology, and rapid resolution after benzathine penicillin G.
rationale: 40-year-old man with painless penile chancre, palmar papules ('acral pebbles'), lymphadenopathy, positive TPHA (1:1200) and VDRL (1:4 after partial treatment), plasma-cell dermal infiltrate, and rapid resolution with benzathine penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 42-year-old female with luetic endolymphatic hydrops (otosyphilis).

evidence_items.source_quote: Results revealed the patient's RPR and fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption test to be positive. Furthermore, a history of syphilis was confirmed. Following a course of 2.4 million units of Benzathine Penicillin G and Prednisone for three weeks, the patient reported improvement in hearing.

rationale: 42-year-old woman with luetic endolymphatic hydrops (sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus) with dual positive RPR and FTA-ABS serology and audiometric/DPOAE recovery following Benzathine Penicillin G and Prednisone. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 56-year-old male with palatal perforation due to tertiary syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood investigations revealed a positive reactive Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) test. Dark field microscopy was done which revealed characteristic cork-screw shaped Treponema pallidium organisms, that confirmed the diagnosis of syphilis.

rationale: 56-year-old man with mid-palatal perforation (gumma), reactive VDRL, and darkfield microscopy demonstrating characteristic corkscrew-shaped Treponema pallidum (E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 43-year-old man with tabetic arthropathy revealing neurosyphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The diagnosis was confirmed by the presence of positive syphilis serology in the blood, the joint fluid and the cerebrospinal fluid. The patient was treated by penicillin G.
evidence_items.test_name: Syphilis serology in blood, joint fluid, and CSF

rationale: 43-year-old man with painless Charcot arthropathy of the right knee (tabetic arthropathy) confirmed by positive syphilis serology in blood, joint fluid, and CSF, treated with penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 35-year-old HIV-positive man with overlapping primary and psoriasiform secondary syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Syphilis serologic examination results showed positive VDRL with titer 1: 128 and TPHA.

rationale: 35-year-old HIV-positive man with generalized psoriasiform plaques involving palms and soles, diffuse alopecia, and penile ulcers, confirmed by high-titer VDRL (1:128) and positive TPHA (E2 secondary syphilis syndrome), improving rapidly after benzathine penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 32-year-old heterosexual male with secondary pulmonary syphilis diagnosed by mNGS in BALF.

evidence_items.source_quote: The TP passive particle agglutination assay (TPPA) was positive, and the toluidine red unheated serum test (TRUST) revealed titer of 1:64.
The mNGS analysis of the BALF identified 56 sequence reads uniquely corresponding to the T. pallidum genome, with 0.37% coverage (Figure 3).
The TRUST titer decreased to 1:16.

rationale: 32-year-old man with palmoplantar erythematous papular rash, left lower lobe pneumonia, positive TPPA, TRUST 1:64, and mNGS detection of Treponema pallidum genome in BALF (E1 confirmatory molecular detection), with pulmonary and 4-fold TRUST (1:16) response to benzathine penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 49-year-old woman with HIV-1 (CD4 482) and tertiary syphilis (gummas and papillitis).

evidence_items.source_quote: Rapid plasma reagin (RPR) test was positive (titer = 1 : 256, normal < 1 : 16).
Tertiary syphilis diagnosis was made on the basis of the skin findings of gummas and papillitis, a manifestation of neurosyphilis.
She was treated with intravenous Penicillin G 5 MU IVI 6 hourly for 2 weeks. Healing occurred with atrophic scaring (Figures 3 and 4).

rationale: 49-year-old HIV-1 positive woman presenting with cutaneous gummas and unilateral acute papillitis. RPR was strongly positive at 1:256 and lesions healed with atrophic scarring after 2 weeks of IV Penicillin G. Meets E2_HIGHLY_CHARACTERISTIC for tertiary syphilis with HIV coinfection (treponemal confirmatory assay not explicitly named, hence MEDIUM confidence). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Preterm female neonate is the primary patient with congenital syphilis and E. cloacae sepsis; metadata age 35.0 reflects mother's age.

evidence_items.source_quote: With noted hepatosplenomegaly and worsening inflammatory markers (CRP 122.9 mg/L), we requested the syphilis test for the newborn and the mother, which later confirmed the diagnosis of congenital syphilis, with infant's RPR 1 : 32 (fourfold the mother's RPR 1 : 8, given in Table 3).
For serological follow-up, the infant's RPR titer decreased fourfold since the age of 1 month and remained at 1 : 8 at 3 months (Table 3).

rationale: Preterm female neonate with Enterobacter cloacae early-onset sepsis and congenital syphilis coinfection. Infant RPR was 1:32 (fourfold higher than maternal RPR 1:8) with hepatosplenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, and 4-fold RPR decline after 10-day IV Benzyl-Penicillin. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Case text documents the 29-year-old mother's syphilis seroconversion during pregnancy (metadata 34.0/Male reflects premature baby boy born at 34 weeks).

evidence_items.source_quote: The pregnant woman went to the hospital for prenatal care at 16 weeks 1/7 days of pregnancy, and serological tests for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and syphilis by chemiluminescent immunoassay (CLIA) were negative.

The pregnant woman went to the hospital for prenatal care at 32 weeks 4/7 days of pregnancy, and the treponemal serological test (CLIA) was positive. The toluidine red unheated serum test (TRUST) titer was 1:16.
evidence_items.test_name: Syphilis CLIA and TRUST (32 weeks 4/7 days)

rationale: 29-year-old pregnant woman who seroconverted during pregnancy: syphilis CLIA was negative at 16 weeks, she developed a non-itchy maculopapular rash at 24 weeks, and at 32w4d had positive CLIA and TRUST 1:16 (husband also CLIA+ and TRUST 1:32). Documented seroconversion + dual reactivity (E1) -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Newborn male infant (text uses 'his'/'he'; metadata lists Female).

evidence_items.source_quote: After admission, the infant received an intravenous penicillin G solution (50,000 units/kg per 6 h) for 10 days and was then re-examined for syphilis. The treponemal serological test (CLIA) was positive, the TRUST titer was 1:16, and he was discharged home with his parents.

When the infant was 6 months old, his parents brought him to the hospital for follow-up. His growth and development indicators were similar to those of normal children. The treponemal serological test was positive, and the TRUST was negative.

rationale: Preterm newborn male delivered at 34w1d to mother with gestational syphilis seroconversion; abstract explicitly describes fetal T. pallidum infection. Infant had positive CLIA and TRUST 1:16, received 10 days IV penicillin G, and TRUST seroreverted to negative by 6 months. E2_HIGHLY_CHARACTERISTIC -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 29-year-old male with newly diagnosed HIV (CD4 358) and neurosyphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: On day 3 of hospital stay, the RPR came back as reactive with a titer of 1:4 and the HIV test came back as positive. The RPR was confirmed by fluorscent treponema antigen antibodies.
Once desensitization was completed, the patient was started on aqueous penicillin G 4 million units q 4 h for a total of 14 days of therapy based on the diagnosis of neurosyphilis.
evidence_items.test_name: Neurosyphilis diagnosis and IV penicillin G response

rationale: 29-year-old male with headache, meningismus, right facial paralysis, and CSF pleocytosis (580 WBC/uL, protein 270 mg/dL). Serum RPR was reactive (1:4) and confirmed by FTA-ABS; improved on 14-day IV aqueous penicillin G for neurosyphilis. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 62-year-old male (Case 1 of 3) with cerebral syphilitic gumma.

evidence_items.source_quote: Postoperative pathology showed infiltration of many plasma cells, lymphocytes, and neutrophils. The lymphocyte infiltration was sleeve-like around the blood vessels (Figure 2A).
The results were as follows: cerebral blood WBC (2 x 106/L), GLU (5.28 mmol/L), Cl (119 mmol/L), negative RPR, and positive TPPA. The symptoms were relieved after anti-syphilitic treatment.

step10_contradiction_notes: RPR was negative while TPPA was positive; resolved in favor of cerebral syphilitic gumma based on histopathology and symptom relief after anti-syphilitic treatment.
rationale: 62-year-old male with frontal lobe mass resected and pathologically confirmed as cerebral syphilitic gumma (plasma cell/lymphocyte perivascular cuffing), positive TPPA (negative RPR), and symptom resolution after anti-syphilitic therapy. Matches E2 tertiary gummatous syphilis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 66-year-old male (Case 2 of 3) with cerebral syphilitic gumma; case_text also appends Case 3 (37-year-old male).

evidence_items.source_quote: Examination of the blood and cerebrospinal fluid indicated positive TPPA (+) and positive RPR (+) tests. The patient was administered with anti-syphilitic treatment.
evidence_items.test_name: Blood and CSF TPPA and RPR

evidence_items.source_quote: Pathological examination indicated argyrophilic staining, with no finding of T. pallidum (Figure 2B).

step10_contradiction_notes: Argyrophilic staining did not visualize T. pallidum spirochetes, but blood and CSF TPPA and RPR were both positive with gumma histopathology.
rationale: 66-year-old male with frontal lobe cerebral syphilitic gumma confirmed by positive TPPA and positive RPR in both blood and CSF, gumma pathology, and anti-syphilitic treatment. E1 confirmatory -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 54-year-old HIV-positive male with spinal syphilitic gumma (Brown-Sequard syndrome) and prior treated syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: At this point, syphilis serological testing was undertaken; this suggested highly active acute infection (serum EIA positive and rapid plasma reagin (RPR) (1 in 64)). CSF serology showed positive Treponema pallidum particle agglutination (TPPA) 10240 and RPR 1 in 2 suggesting active disease.

Due to no conclusive TB diagnosis, concurrent neurosyphilis treatment was initiated by way of 14-day high-dose benzylpenicillin therapy commencing on day 11 of presentation. Repeat MRI of the spine on days 12 and 22 of admission revealed incremental improvement in both spinal cord oedema and the size of the T4-T5 lesions (Figure 1).

rationale: 54-year-old HIV-positive man presenting with Brown-Sequard syndrome and T4-T5 spinal syphilitic gumma. Serum EIA positive, RPR 1:64; CSF TPPA 1:10240, RPR 1:2 with CSF pleocytosis and marked clinical/MRI improvement on 14-day IV benzylpenicillin. E1 confirmatory -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 82-year-old male with syphilitic aortitis and aortic arch aneurysm.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 86-year-old male with atypical annular secondary syphilis.

E1 confirmatory -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 30-year-old man with primary rectal syphilis mimicking rectal cancer

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 46-year-old male worker with spinal syphilitic gumma

rationale: 46-year-old man with T7 intramedullary spinal syphilitic gumma. Positive TPPA and TRUST (serum 1:128, CSF 1:32) with CSF pleocytosis (120/uL) and complete clinical/MRI resolution and >=4-fold TRUST drop (to 1:4 serum, 1:1 CSF) after IV penicillin G.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 43-year-old Hispanic male with HIV/AIDS, neurosyphilis, cryptococcal meningitis, and TB meningitis

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 29-year-old Malay pregnant woman (metadata gender Male is erroneous) with syphilis reinfection in pregnancy

evidence_items.source_quote: However, the rapid plasma reagin (RPR) was reactive at 1:16 titration. The diagnosis of syphilis was confirmed by a positive Syphilis IgG result.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 41-year-old male with secondary syphilis and syphilitic hepatitis

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 38-year-old female with syphilitic uveitis and obstructive retinal vasculitis

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 37-year-old Caucasian male with HIV and non-primary nail-plate syphilis

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Japanese male neonate (born at 36w2d to 29-year-old mother) with congenital syphilis

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 2-week-old male infant with congenital syphilis

rationale: 2-week-old male infant with congenital syphilis presenting with palmoplantar keratoderma, snuffles, and hepatosplenomegaly. Confirmed by infant VDRL 1:256 + TPHA positive, maternal VDRL 1:16 + TPHA positive, and VDRL drop to 1:2 after IV aqueous crystalline penicillin (E1). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 28-year-old male with secondary syphilis and HIV coinfection

evidence_items.source_quote: The results of venereal disease research laboratory test (VDRL) and treponema pallidum particle agglutination assay (TPHA) examinations were positive (positive at 1: 256 and 1: 10240).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 55-year-old man with tertiary syphilis mimicking tongue squamous cell carcinoma

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 66-year-old man with poorly treated bilateral acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis (ASPPC) complicated by CNV

started systemic treatment with intravenous Penicillin G for 14 days as well as intravitreal ranibizumab injections on the RE in a PRN regimen.
After systemic and intravitreal treatment, the patient experienced visual acuity improvement to 20/25, without metamorphopsia. There was a regression of the RPE detachment and cystoid macular edema

rationale: 66-year-old man with active bilateral acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis (ASPPC) complicated by CNV, positive TPHA, history of inadequate oral antibiotic treatment 30 years prior, and regression of RPE detachment/CME after 14 days of IV Penicillin G (E2). Negative VDRL resolved in context of late ocular syphilis. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 48-year-old Caucasian heterosexual man admitted with atrial fibrillation, chest pain, and ascending aortic aneurysm.

evidence_items.source_quote: A wrinkling wall with tree bark aspect, suggesting an inflammatory aortitis (luetic), was noticeable.
We tested the patient, and the venereal disease research laboratory test (VDRL) was intensely positive, as were the Treponema pallidum hemagglutination test (TPHA) and rapid plasma reagin (RPR).

Our suspicion was confirmed through histological examination of the aortic wall, revealing obliterating endarteritis of the vasa vasorum, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, mesoaortitis with reduction in the musculo-elastic medial tissue (Figure 2A and B).
The polymerase chain reaction did not reveal traces of living treponemal spirochetes.

step10_contradiction_notes: Aortic wall PCR was negative for living treponemal spirochetes and CSF was normal, which is expected in late tertiary syphilitic aortitis and does not refute the diagnosis established by tree-barking aortitis, intensely positive VDRL/RPR/TPHA, and characteristic mesoaortitis histology.
rationale: 48-year-old male with impending rupture of a 78 mm ascending aortic aneurysm showing intraoperative 'tree bark' wrinkling, intensely positive VDRL, RPR, and TPHA, and histopathologic obliterating endarteritis of the vasa vasorum with lymphoplasmacytic mesoaortitis (E2 tertiary syphilitic aortitis). Negative PCR for living spirochetes is compatible with late tertiary disease. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 28-year-old male presenting with RUQ abdominal pain, elevated LFTs, and painless penile chancre.

evidence_items.test_name: Prior RPR and T. pallidum total antibody

evidence_items.source_quote: In addition, he had a positive RPR screen with titers of 32 dils along with a positive treponema IgM/IgG antibody.
evidence_items.test_name: RPR titer and Treponema IgM/IgG serology (documented seroconversion)

evidence_items.source_quote: A painless chancre was noted on the ventral aspect of the penile shaft without any obvious discharge.

step10_contradiction_notes: RPR 6 months prior and T. pallidum total antibody 1 month prior were negative, representing documented seroconversion rather than a contradiction.
rationale: 28-year-old male with syphilitic hepatitis, painless penile chancre, and documented seroconversion from negative RPR (6 months prior) and negative T. pallidum total antibody (1 month prior) to RPR 1:32 and positive Treponema IgM/IgG (E1 confirmatory dual reactivity with seroconversion). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 43-year-old black man presenting with confusion, memory loss, and mesiotemporal T2/FLAIR hyperintensity.

evidence_items.source_quote: The results of the serum rapid plasma reagent (RPR) test (titer, 1 : 256) and serum Treponema pallidum haemagglutination (TPHA) test (titer, 1 : 20480) were positive. CSF TPHA titer was 1 : 10240 and Venereal Disease Research Laboratory test (VDRL) titer was 1 : 32. rationale: 25-year-old male with left optic neuritis diagnosed with neurosyphilis. Blood VDRL, TPHA (1:1280), and RPR (1:64) were positive, and CSF-VDRL, CSF-TPHA (1:80), and CSF-RPR were reactive with lymphocytic pleocytosis (E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 50-year-old Caucasian male with HIV and penicillin allergy presenting with bilateral papilledema and anterior uveitis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood samples showed reactive rapid plasma regain (RPR) with a 1 : 128 titer and positive IgG Treponema pallidum antibody (TPA).
Lumbar puncture revealed CSF with 18% PMNs but was negative for VDRL.
After 13 months from initial presentation, his RPR titer was nonreactive, confirming a successful treatment.

step10_contradiction_notes: CSF-VDRL was negative, but ocular syphilis is confirmed by serum RPR 1:128, positive IgG TPA, characteristic bilateral optic nerve edema/anterior uveitis, Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, and complete resolution with RPR becoming nonreactive after IV Penicillin G.
rationale: 50-year-old male with HIV presenting with bilateral optic nerve head edema, retinal hemorrhage, and anterior uveitis. Serum RPR was 1:128 with positive IgG TPA (E2), and he responded to IV Penicillin G with RPR becoming nonreactive at 13 months. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 59-year-old woman with pulmonary syphilis mimicking hematogenous metastases.

evidence_items.source_quote: A preoperative laboratory screening showed the rapid plasma reagin (RPR) and venereal disease research laboratory (VDRL) tests to be positive. These were followed by more specific treponemal tests; the Treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay (TPHA) (titer, 1:302) was positive and the fluorescent Treponemal antibody absorption (FTA-ABS) test was negative for IgM and positive for IgG. Therefore, a clinical diagnosis of syphilis was made.

The histologic examination of a left inguinal lymph node specimen showed a negative Warthin Starry silver stain, but revealed hyperplasia of secondary lymphoid follicles and extensive plasma cell proliferation on hematoxylin-eosin stain, suggesting possible syphilis [Figure 3].
evidence_items.test_name: Lymph node Warthin-Starry stain and H&E

evidence_items.source_quote: Two months after discharge, the patient returned for a follow-up evaluation and a CT scan showed complete disappearance of the pulmonary nodules [Figure 4B] with a further reduction in the size of the involved lymph nodes.

step10_contradiction_notes: Warthin-Starry silver stain of the inguinal lymph node was negative, but syphilis was confirmed by positive RPR/VDRL, TPHA (1:302), FTA-ABS IgG, plasma cell-rich lymphadenitis, and complete resolution of pulmonary nodules after IM penicillin G.
rationale: 59-year-old woman with pulmonary nodules and inguinal lymphadenopathy diagnosed as pulmonary syphilis. RPR, VDRL, TPHA (1:302), and FTA-ABS IgG were positive, and pulmonary nodules completely resolved after IM penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 45-year-old man with acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis (ASPPC).

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory results returned negative for QuantiFERON-TB testing, and positive for venereal disease research laboratory test and fluorescent treponemal antibody testing. Therefore, a definite diagnosis of ASPPC was made, and the patient was promptly referred to the Infectious Disease Department for systemic treatment with penicillin.

rationale: 45-year-old man presenting with macular placoid lesion diagnosed as acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis (ASPPC) with positive VDRL and fluorescent treponemal antibody testing (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Preterm male infant (31 weeks gestation) with congenital syphilis; mother had reactive CMIA, TPPA, and RPR 1:32.

evidence_items.source_quote: Placental pathology showed innumerable spirochetes but a lack of inflammation or necrosis (Figure 1). The infant's serum RPR titer was 1:16.

syphilis serology screen using chemiluminescent microparticle immunoassay (CMIA) was completed, and the screen was positive1. The confirmatory T. pallidum particulate agglutination assay (TPPA) was also reactive and the rapid plasma reagin (RPR) showed a titer of 1:32.
The CSF sample was negative by the venereal disease research laboratory (VDRL) test and indeterminate by the fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption (FTA-ABS) test.

step10_contradiction_notes: Bloody neonatal CSF sample (1 week after birth, after starting IV penicillin) was VDRL-negative and FTA-ABS indeterminate, but congenital syphilis was confirmed by innumerable spirochetes on placental pathology, infant RPR 1:16, maternal CMIA/TPPA/RPR 1:32, and classic long bone metaphyseal bands.
rationale: Preterm male infant (31 weeks' gestation) with non-immune hydrops fetalis and hepatic dysfunction due to congenital syphilis. Confirmed by innumerable spirochetes on placental pathology (E1), infant serum RPR 1:16, maternal CMIA/TPPA/RPR 1:32, and classic long bone x-rays. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 51-year-old HIV-positive transgender woman with papulonodular secondary syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory data were remarkable for an RPR titer of 1: 256.
Immunohistochemistry for T. pallidum was positive in all 3 biopsies (Fig. 2). A diagnosis of papulonodular syphilis was established.
evidence_items.test_name: T. pallidum immunohistochemistry on skin biopsies

rationale: 51-year-old transgender woman with HIV presenting with papulonodular secondary syphilis. Serum RPR was 1:256 and Treponema pallidum immunohistochemistry was positive in all 3 skin biopsies (E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 35-year-old man with acquired syphilis (Tullio phenomenon/otosyphilis) and concurrent HIV.

evidence_items.source_quote: Rapid plasma reagin (RPR) was positive at a titer of 1:128 and was confirmed by a fluorescent treponemal antibody test.
Cerebrospinal fluid venereal disease research laboratory test (CSF-VDRL) results were negative.

step10_contradiction_notes: CSF-VDRL was negative despite 8 leukocytes/microL in CSF, but acquired syphilis (otosyphilis with Tullio phenomenon) is confirmed by serum RPR 1:128 and positive FTA-ABS.
rationale: 35-year-old man presenting with headaches, hearing loss, and Tullio phenomenon, concurrently diagnosed with HIV and acquired syphilis. Serum RPR was 1:128 with confirmatory FTA-ABS positive (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 38-year-old Indian man with secondary syphilis and pleural effusion.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic testing was also performed and was positive for Treponema pallidum antibody, and RPR was reactive 1 : 1. Inno-lia syphilis confirmatory test was also positive.
evidence_items.test_name: T. pallidum antibody, RPR, and INNO-LIA confirmatory test

rationale: 38-year-old man presenting with pleurisy, pleural effusion, and macular rash on feet/shins diagnosed as pulmonary/secondary syphilis based on positive T. pallidum antibody, reactive RPR (1:1), and positive INNO-LIA confirmatory test (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 74-year-old man with squamous cell carcinoma arising on a syphilitic gumma of the hard palate.

evidence_items.source_quote: His erythrocyte sedimentation rate was raised, venereal disease research laboratory (VDRL) was 1:1 and treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay was positive. His cerebrospinal fluid VDRL and HIV were negative.
There was also a perforation of 1.5 cm x 1 cm over the hard palate with induration and sloughing at the margins [Figure 2].

rationale: 74-year-old man with palatal perforation from a syphilitic gumma (complicated by SCC) and syphilitic leukoplakia. VDRL was 1:1, TPHA was positive, and he was treated with doxycycline for 28 days (E2 late tertiary syphilis). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 45-year-old HIV-infected male with oral secondary syphilis (plaques en prairie fauchee and split papule).

evidence_items.source_quote: Secondary syphilis had been fully and successfully treated 8 years earlier and previous Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) assays were negative.
A novel VDRL assay was performed and yielded a titer of 1/128. Fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption tests were reactive for IgG and IgM.

rationale: 45-year-old HIV-infected male with oral secondary syphilis (plaques en prairie fauchee, split papule). Documented seroconversion from prior negative VDRL to VDRL 1:128 and reactive FTA-ABS IgG/IgM (E1 confirmatory), with rapid resolution after IM benzathine penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 37-year-old MSM patient with concurrent Monkeypox, HIV, and secondary syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology examination was positive for syphilis (VDRL 1:1024), and also reactive for HIV (rapid test and immunoassay); tests for hepatitis B and C were non-reactive; RT-PCR assay for MP was positive.

rationale: 37-year-old MSM patient presenting with vesicular/pustular lesions, cervical lymphadenopathy, and fever, found to have Monkeypox (PCR+), HIV, and concurrent secondary syphilis with VDRL 1:1024 (E2) treated with benzathine penicillin. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 28-year-old woman with anaplastic oligodendroglioma and concurrent syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The toluidine red unheated serum test (TRUST) titer was 1:8. The Treponema pallidum particle agglutination test (TPPA) was 1:80 positive, and serology was negative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
Her CSF analysis revealed that TRUST was negative and TPPA was 1:40 positive.

step10_contradiction_notes: Post-treatment CSF TRUST was negative and the frontal lobe mass proved to be anaplastic oligodendroglioma rather than cerebral gumma, but systemic syphilis comorbidity was affirmed by dual serum TRUST (1:8) + TPPA (1:80), CSF TPPA (1:40), and 14-day IV penicillin G therapy.
rationale: 28-year-old woman diagnosed with both anaplastic oligodendroglioma and syphilis. Serum TRUST (1:8) and TPPA (1:80) were positive, CSF TPPA was 1:40 positive, and she received 14 days of IV penicillin G (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 56-year-old male with well-controlled HIV presenting with syphilitic alopecia, palmar/plantar plaques, and ocular syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory workup showed strongly positive RPR at 1 : 256. A positive MHA-TP (Microhemagglutination Assay for Treponemal palladium Antibodies) confirmed the diagnosis of syphilis.

rationale: 56-year-old male with HIV presenting with desquamating palmar/plantar plaques (Biett collarettes), alopecia, and uveitis. RPR was 1:256 with positive MHA-TP (E2) and complete resolution after 2 weeks of IV Penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 46-year-old man presenting with psychotic mania as solitary manifestation of neurosyphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: However, the patient showed a positive result for the serum venereal disease research laboratory (VDRL) test, at a titer of 1:32. Fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption test showed reactivity, whereas results of the HIV test were negative.

On the 3rd day, analysis of cerebrospinal fluid through a lumbar puncture showed a positive VDRL result, at a titer of 1:8, and increased white blood cell count (22/mm3) and total protein (78.7 mg/dL). Since a positive VDRL result for the cerebrospinal fluid confirmed the diagnosis of neurosyphilis, the patient was administered intravenous penicillin G, 20 million units daily, for 2 weeks.

rationale: 46-year-old man with acute psychotic mania diagnosed with neurosyphilis. Serum VDRL (1:32) and FTA-ABS were reactive, and CSF-VDRL was reactive at 1:8 with CSF pleocytosis (E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 16-year-old female sex worker with solitary interdigital condyloma latum of secondary syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Immunohistochemistry revealed numerous spirochetes within the epidermis (Figure 4). Both the toluidine red unheated serum test (TRUST) and Treponema pallidum hemagglutination test were positive; the TRUST test results were positive at a dilution of 1:64.
evidence_items.test_name: Skin biopsy spirochete IHC, TRUST, and TPHA

rationale: 16-year-old female presenting with solitary interdigital condyloma latum. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated numerous spirochetes in the epidermis (E1 confirmatory), and both TRUST (1:64) and TPHA were positive, with lesion resolution and TRUST drop to 1:4 after benzathine penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 35-year-old man with HIV stage II, secondary syphilis (palatal mucous patches, papules), ocular syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay (TPHA) titer was reactive with titer 1:10,240, and quantitative venereal disease research laboratory test (VDRL) was reactive with titer 1:256.
Intraoral examination showed irregular painless multiple ulcers on the palate with white margins, and yellow reddish base (Figure 1).

rationale: 35-year-old man with HIV stage II referred with secondary syphilis (palatal mucous patches and cutaneous papules) and ocular syphilis. TPHA was reactive at 1:10,240 and quantitative VDRL was reactive at 1:256 (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 29-year-old man with HIV stage IV and latent syphilis.

evidence_items.source_quote: He was diagnosed by the Internist with HIV stage IV with wasting syndrome, hypothyroidism, latent syphilis, chronic hepatitis B, moderate dehydration et causa inadequate intake, stage 1 acute kidney injury (AKI), inflammatory anemia, and malnutrition.
Laboratory examinations showed reactive TPHA with titer 1:5120 and reactive VDRL with titer 1:64, reactive hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg), reactive HBsAg, non-reactive anti-hepatitis c virus (HCV).

rationale: 29-year-old man with HIV stage IV diagnosed by the Internist with latent syphilis. Laboratory testing showed reactive TPHA (1:5120) and high-titer reactive VDRL (1:64) (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 38-year-old male with secondary syphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: Physical examination revealed diffuse lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and the presence of reddish wartlike sores over the glans penis.

Blood investigations showed a positive venereal disease research laboratory test (VDRL). Treponema pallidum particle agglutination assay (TP-PA) was positive for T. pallidum specific immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody.

rationale: A 38-year-old man presented with 5 weeks of fever, weight loss, patchy alopecia, diffuse lymphadenopathy, and wartlike sores on the glans penis. Both VDRL and confirmatory TP-PA were positive, establishing active secondary syphilis.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 40-year-old male with neurosyphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: Among serum serological tests, Treponema Pallidum hemagglutination assay (TPHA) was positive at 1/2560 dilution. Venereal Diseases Research Laboratories (VDRL) and Rapid Plasma Reagin (RPR) tests were also positive.
In serologic examination of CSF, fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption (FTA- ABS) and VDRL was positive at 1/2 and TPHA at 1/10240 dilutions.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF-VDRL, CSF FTA-ABS, and CSF TPHA

rationale: A 40-year-old man with neuropsychiatric decline and pupillary abnormalities had reactive CSF-VDRL (1:2), CSF FTA-ABS, and CSF TPHA (1:10240) alongside positive serum VDRL, RPR, and TPHA (1:2560), confirming neurosyphilis (E1).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 36-year-old male with snail track ulcers of secondary syphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: Oral findings showed irregular erythematous patches on the dorsum of the tongue and erosive plaques on the tongue left margin with snail track pattern.
The laboratory tests were positive for TPHA VDRL (1/64), and negative for HIV, hepatitis B and C. The diagnosis of snail track ulcers of secondary syphilis was performed.

rationale: A 36-year-old male presented with characteristic snail track ulcers of the tongue, diffuse micropolyadenomegaly, high-titer VDRL (1/64), and positive TPHA, confirming secondary syphilis (E2) with complete resolution after benzathine penicillin.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 36-year-old female with tertiary syphilitic hepatitis and hepatic gummas

evidence_items.source_quote: however, the patient tested positive for Treponema pallidum antibodies (titer of 1:1,024)

While a Warthin-Starry stain on the sample was negative, immunohistochemistry for treponemal organisms confirmed the presence of Treponema pallidum (Biocare APA 135 AA) and the diagnosis of tertiary stage SH with hepatic gummas (Figure 3B).

step10_contradiction_notes: Warthin-Starry stain on liver biopsy was negative, but specific Treponema pallidum immunohistochemistry (IHC) was positive, confirming syphilitic hepatitis with hepatic gummas.
rationale: A 36-year-old woman presenting with seizures and multiple hepatic lesions had positive T. pallidum antibodies (1:1,024) and confirmatory T. pallidum immunohistochemistry on liver biopsy (E1), establishing tertiary syphilitic hepatitis with hepatic gummas.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 15-year-old girl with neurosyphilis presenting with psychosis and parkinsonism

evidence_items.source_quote: The VDRL serum test yielded positive results with respect to the T. pallidum antibody (TPA); we then found a titer of 1:4 with respect to the toluidine red unheated serum test (TRUST), and we obtained positive results on the T. pallidum particle-agglutination test.
A lumbar puncture was then performed under the suspicion that the patient had neurosyphilis, and the results showed that the cerebral spinal fluid VDRL was 1:2 (reactive)

rationale: A 15-year-old girl with psychosis and parkinsonism had positive serum VDRL, TRUST (1:4), and TP-PA, plus a reactive CSF-VDRL (1:2) (E1 confirmatory), and improved markedly after intravenous and intramuscular penicillin therapy.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 83-year-old female with neurosyphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: Patient's RPR quantitative was found to be 1:8 and FTA-Ab was reactive. The patient was diagnosed with neurosyphilis and notified with referral to follow-up with infectious disease as an outpatient.
The patient completed 2 weeks of antibiotics for neurosyphilis at home with home health. Patient returned to prior baseline following completion of treatment.
evidence_items.test_name: Therapeutic response to Penicillin G / Ceftriaxone

rationale: An 83-year-old woman with altered mental status and intermittent ataxia had reactive quantitative RPR (1:8) and FTA-Ab, was diagnosed with neurosyphilis (LP unsuccessful), and returned to baseline after IV penicillin G and ceftriaxone.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 29-year-old pregnant woman with early latent syphilis and congenital syphilis in the fetus

evidence_items.source_quote: The diagnosis of syphilis was performed only during antenatal screening in the first trimester by a positive venereal disease research laboratory (VDRL) and a treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay (TPHA) title of 1:2560.

Maternal blood tests for cytomegalovirus, coxsackievirus, parvovirus, toxoplasma, and herpes virus types 1 and 2 were found negative while syphilis serologic tests were confirmed positive with RPR title 1:4 and TPHA title 1:640.

The research of Treponema Pallidum with coloring of Warthin-Starry identified images compatible with the morphological appearance of the germ. The diagnostic conclusion deposed for congenital syphilis.

rationale: A 29-year-old pregnant woman had positive VDRL/RPR (1:4) and TPHA (1:2560 -> 1:640), and despite benzathine penicillin G therapy developed fetal hydrops/hydrocephalus; fetal autopsy confirmed congenital syphilis via Warthin-Starry silver stain (E1).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 40-year-old male with drug-induced hepatitis and active secondary syphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient's rapid plasma reagin was reactive with a titer of 1:512. Treponema pallidum particle agglutination was reactive as well.
A final diagnosis of drug-induced acute hepatitis from methamphetamine, oxycodone/acetaminophen and buprenorphine in the setting of secondary syphilis and an occult HBV infection was made.
He presented to the Infectious Disease Clinic for a 6-month follow up in May 2013 with a 64-fold decline in rapid plasma reagin titer to 1:8.

step10_contradiction_notes: Liver biopsy ruled out syphilitic hepatitis (hepatitis was drug-induced), but active secondary syphilis itself was confirmed as a concurrent comorbidity.
rationale: A 40-year-old man presented with papulosquamous lesions on palms, soles, penis, and scrotum, oral ulcer, RPR 1:512, and reactive TP-PA, with a 64-fold RPR decline after benzathine penicillin G. While his hepatitis was drug-induced, active secondary syphilis is a confirmed comorbidity (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 63-year-old hemodialyzed man with tertiary syphilis and syphilitic uveitis

evidence_items.source_quote: VDRL = 2, TPHA 1280, FTA abs 100, FTA -M <10 and positive anti -TpN47, TmpA, TpN17 and TpN 15(IgG western-blot).
evidence_items.test_name: VDRL, TPHA, FTA-ABS, and T. pallidum IgG Western blot

evidence_items.source_quote: Funduscopic appearance showed beside proliferative retinopathy, a syphilitic uveitis thereafter, discovered incidentally elsewhere.

The patient received an empirical treatment of ceftriaxone 1.5 gr administered post-dialysis with a spectacular response within one week; therapy judged by net improvement of his weakness and return home walking.

rationale: A 63-year-old hemodialyzed man with progressive lower-limb weakness had reactive VDRL, TPHA (1280), FTA-ABS (100), and T. pallidum IgG Western blot, plus syphilitic uveitis and dramatic motor recovery on ceftriaxone, confirming active tertiary syphilis (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 35-year-old HIV-positive male with syphilitic aortic aneurysm

evidence_items.source_quote: Further laboratory studies were notable for a strongly positive Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) titer of 1 : 128 and a positive fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption (FTA-ABS) test.

On histopathological examination of the aorta, the adventitia showed focal cellular infiltrates with a predominance of lymphocytes and the vasa vasorum demonstrated thickening of the intima (Figure 1(d)) strongly suggesting the diagnosis of a syphilitic aortic aneurysm.

rationale: A 35-year-old HIV-positive man presented with a ruptured aortic aneurysm from ascending aorta to iliac vessels, VDRL 1:128, positive FTA-ABS, and autopsy histopathology showing syphilitic aortitis (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 41-year-old HIV-positive male with penile SCC, HBV, and syphilis co-infection

evidence_items.source_quote: However, the results were reactive for syphilis (VDRL reactive 1 in 1 dilution); later confirmed with treponema heamagglutination test and hepatitis B (positive HBs antigen, done by enzyme-linked immunosorbant assay).
For syphilis, the patient was given a single dose of intramuscular injection benzathine penicillin 24 lakh international units after test dose.

step10_contradiction_notes: The penile ulcer itself was histopathologically confirmed as squamous cell carcinoma, while syphilis was diagnosed as a concurrent co-infection (VDRL 1:1 + TPHA positive) and treated with benzathine penicillin.
rationale: A 41-year-old HIV-positive man with penile squamous cell carcinoma had reactive VDRL (1:1) confirmed by TPHA and received intramuscular benzathine penicillin for concurrent syphilis co-infection (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 50-year-old male with cardiovascular syphilis and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum venereal disease research laboratory test was positive in 1:4 dilution. Treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay was positive.

Histopathology revealed elastic tissue degeneration of media and replacement with fibrous tissue, intima shows thinning. Adventitia shows thickening and fibrosis. Vessel wall shows lymphocytes and plasma cell infiltration. Thus, the histopathology is more in favor of syphilitic etiology.

rationale: A 50-year-old male with dissecting thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm and vertebral erosion had positive VDRL (1:4) and TPHA, aortic histopathology favoring syphilitic aortitis (E2), and received 20 days of IM procaine penicillin.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 33-year-old male with ocular syphilis (panuveitis) and HIV

evidence_items.source_quote: RPR (1:32) and TPHA (1:640) were positive. ELISA and Western Blot test for HIV were also positive, with a CD4 count of 187 cells/mul (normal 383-1347 cells/mul).
He was administered intravenous penicillin G 24 million units/day for 14 days, and intramuscular benzathine penicillin 2.4 million units weekly for three weeks.
evidence_items.test_name: Penicillin G therapy for ocular syphilis

rationale: A 33-year-old man with panuveitis had high-titer RPR (1:32) and TPHA (1:640) (E2), concurrent HIV diagnosis, and visual improvement following 14 days of IV penicillin G and 3 weekly doses of IM benzathine penicillin.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 71-year-old woman with neurosyphilitic Charcot arthropathy of left knee and ankle.

evidence_items.source_quote: The Treponema pallidum hemagglutination test was positive.
The patient had an HbA1c level of 6.1% and a fasting glucose level of 103 mg/dL; the patient was not considered to have diabetes. Syringomyelia was not observed on whole-spine MRI.

rationale: 71-year-old female with severe neurosyphilitic Charcot arthropathy of the left knee and ankle, positive TPHA, and exclusion of diabetes and syringomyelia. Tertiary neurosyphilitic complication -> POSITIVE (MEDIUM confidence as nontreponemal titer/CSF-VDRL not reported).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 35-year-old man with HIV, primary mpox, and secondary syphilis co-infection.

evidence_items.source_quote: He had also developed a new diffuse maculopapular rash on the neck, chest, and torso with a herald patch on the right chest (Image 3).

Co-infection testing eventually revealed reactive syphilis antibody, reactive Fluorescent Treponemal Antibody Absorption test, and reactive Rapid Plasma Reagin test (RPR) with titer 1:1. Through California Reportable Disease Information Exchange, no prior treatment history for syphilis was found. Syphilis was staged as secondary syphilis.
He was treated with 2.4 million units of benzathine penicillin G intramuscularly once.

rationale: 35-year-old HIV+ male with mpox co-infected with secondary syphilis, confirmed by dual reactivity (reactive syphilis antibody, reactive FTA-ABS, reactive RPR 1:1) with no prior syphilis treatment history, diffuse maculopapular rash, and resolution after IM benzathine penicillin G -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 33-year-old female with secondary syphilis and Sweet syndrome.

evidence_items.source_quote: Syphilis serology demonstrated a Venereal Disease Research Laboratory test result of 1:32, a positive treponemal IgM/IgG antibody test, and a positive Treponema pallidum hemagglutination test.

The patient was treated with weekly intramuscular injections of 2.4 million units of benzathine penicillin over a period of 4 weeks, followed by treatment with tapering doses of systemic prednisone (1 mg/kg/day which were gradually tapered within 2 weeks). The tonsillar lesions and the rash resolved without scarring, but with little residual pigmentation.
evidence_items.test_name: Benzathine penicillin G therapy and clinical resolution

rationale: 33-year-old female with acute necrotizing tonsillitis, Sweet syndrome, and secondary syphilis confirmed by VDRL 1:32, positive treponemal IgM/IgG, and positive TPHA, resolving with benzathine penicillin G -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 54-year-old heterosexual male with intracranial syphilitic gumma.

evidence_items.source_quote: Syphilis serology was strongly positive for both treponemal and non-treponemal specific antibodies with a rapid-plasma regain (RPR) titer of 1:64.
Spirochete immunostaining (Figures 2E,F) highlighted many organisms, typical spiral and thread-like, in the excised lesion.

Eventually, the patient was diagnosed with an intracranial syphilitic gumma and treated with aqueous crystalline penicillin G, 4 million units intravenously every 4 hours for 14 days. At the 3-month follow-up, an 8-fold decrease in the RPR titer was observed.
evidence_items.test_name: Penicillin G therapy and 8-fold RPR titer drop

rationale: 54-year-old male with intracranial syphilitic gumma confirmed by T. pallidum immunostaining of excised brain tissue, dual positive treponemal/nontreponemal serology (RPR 1:64), and 8-fold RPR drop after IV penicillin G -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 52-year-old woman with cerebral syphilitic gumma.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests revealed positive results of the T. pallidum particle agglutination (TPPA) and toluidine red unheated serum test (TRUST), with a TRUST titer of 1:64.

Post-operative pathology (Figure 3) revealed granulation tissue with ischemic necrosis surrounded by multinucleated giant cells, plasmacytes, and lymphocytes. Based on the above findings, the clinical diagnosis of cerebral syphilitic gumma was made. Penicillin treatment (18 million U/day) was given for 2 weeks after the operation, and the patient's symptoms were relieved gradually.
evidence_items.test_name: Brain pathology (gummatous granulomatous lesion) and penicillin response
