rationale: 26-year-old male with AIDS and West Nile virus rhombencephalitis who also had confirmed neurosyphilis: reactive CSF-VDRL (1:1, RBC 3) with positive FTA-ABS and serum RPR 1:16 (E1 confirmatory), treated with 14-day IV penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 34-year-old pregnant woman with untreated gestational syphilis resulting in congenital syphilis in newborn

evidence_items.source_quote: At 10 weeks of her current gestation, the rapid plasma reagin (RPR) test was positive (1:16), and the patient was consulted by an infectious disease specialist. An additional Treponema pallidum Hemagglutination test (TPHA) was taken and came back positive.
Spirochetes were detected in the umbilical cord stroma by the Warthin-Starry method (Figure 3).

step10_contradiction_notes: Maternal CSF-VDRL showed no pathological changes (neurosyphilis excluded in mother), while gestational and congenital syphilis are confirmed.
rationale: 34-year-old pregnant woman with untreated syphilis during pregnancy (RPR 1:16 and TPHA positive at 10 weeks and 33 weeks), resulting in congenital syphilis in the premature neonate (RPR 1:16, TPHA 4+, IgM+) and Warthin-Starry stain detection of spirochetes in the umbilical cord stroma (E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 15-year-old adolescent male with HIV and secondary syphilis following sexual abuse

evidence_items.source_quote: Symmetrical erythematous macules with collarette scales were observed on the palms and soles. Venereological examination showed skin-colored verrucous plaques in the perianal area, ranging from 0.5 cm x 0.5 cm x 0.1 cm to 2 cm x 2 cm x 0.2 cm.
HIV and syphilis tests were positive, with Treponema pallidum Hemagglutination Assay (TPHA) and Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) titer of 1:64.

step10_contradiction_notes: Lumbar puncture ruled out neurosyphilis, while secondary syphilis is confirmed.
rationale: 15-year-old male with palmoplantar macules with collarette scales, perianal verrucous plaques (biopsy consistent with secondary syphilis), high-titer VDRL (1:64), and reactive TPHA (E2), treated with benzathine benzylpenicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 50-year-old female with otosyphilis / neurosyphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: blood tests were positive for both rapid plasma regain (RPR) and Treponema pallidum antibody (TPAb) (Table 1). Subsequently, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis and contrast-enhanced MRI were performed. The CSF analysis revealed an increased mononuclear cell count and elevated protein levels. Further testing yielded positive results for CSF fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption (FTA-ABS) and TPAb (Table 2).
Quantitative RPR testing revealed a gradual decline, reaching less than one-fourth of the pre-treatment level six months after treatment initiation.

rationale: 50-year-old female with acute unilateral sensorineural hearing loss (otosyphilis). Serum RPR and TPAb were positive, CSF showed mononuclear pleocytosis, elevated protein, and positive CSF FTA-ABS and TPAb (E2), with >4-fold RPR decline after ampicillin. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 42-year-old man with serologically confirmed syphilitic chorioretinitis

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient underwent an infectious and inflammatory serological workup and was diagnosed with syphilis. The patient received treatment including intravenous penicillin G (24 million units/per day) for 14 days. Six months later, there was complete regression of the white dots in both eyes, and subsequent IVFA showed resolution of the bilateral disc leakage.

rationale: 42-year-old man with bilateral syphilitic chorioretinitis (vitreous cells, hyperautofluorescent white dots, optic disc leakage). Serological workup established syphilis (confirmed in abstract as serologically confirmed syphilitic chorioretinitis), with complete regression after 14 days of IV penicillin G (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 67-year-old man with serologically confirmed syphilitic chorioretinitis

evidence_items.source_quote: After extensive serological workup, the patient was diagnosed with syphilitic chorioretinitis in the right eye.
One month after treatment with intravenous penicillin G (24 million units/per day for 14 days), there was an improvement in symptoms and chorioretinal lesions (Figure 4).

rationale: 67-year-old man with right-eye syphilitic chorioretinitis (hyperautofluorescent placoid lesion, vitreous inflammation, ellipsoid zone disruption). Diagnosed via extensive serological workup (abstract notes serologically confirmed) and improved after 14 days of IV penicillin G (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 56-year-old man with serologically confirmed bilateral syphilitic chorioretinitis

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient underwent an extensive serological workup, which revealed positive syphilis antibodies. The patient was diagnosed with syphilis. One month after IV penicillin (24 million units/per day for 14 days) treatment, the patient's visual symptoms and clinical findings resolved.
evidence_items.test_name: Syphilis antibody serology and clinical response

rationale: 56-year-old man with bilateral syphilitic chorioretinitis (placoid lesions, white dots, active retinal vasculitis on IVFA). Extensive serological workup revealed positive syphilis antibodies and he was diagnosed with syphilis, resolving after 14 days of IV penicillin (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Female newborn with congenital bullous syphilis (pemphigus syphiliticus)

evidence_items.source_quote: The neonate's RPR was positive at 1:1, and the maternal RPR was also positive at 1:1. The neonatal TPHA titer was 1:2560, mirroring the maternal titer of 1:2560. The newborn tested negative for IgM antibodies, while the mother tested positive.
A diagnosis of congenital bullous syphilis was established. Treatment with aqueous crystalline penicillin G at 100,000 units/kg/day IV was initiated
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical diagnosis and IV penicillin G

step10_contradiction_notes: Newborn IgM was negative, but maternal IgM was positive with documented maternal seroconversion since first trimester, neonatal RPR 1:1 + TPHA 1:2560, plantar bullous lesions, hepatosplenomegaly, luetic metaphysitis, and Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction.
rationale: Female newborn with congenital bullous syphilis (plantar bullae, hepatosplenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, luetic metaphysitis on X-ray). Neonatal/maternal RPR 1:1 and TPHA 1:2560 with maternal IgM+ and documented seroconversion after normal 1st-trimester screen (E1), treated with IV penicillin G. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Male carpenter with tabes dorsalis (neurosyphilis) and Argyll-Robertson pupils

evidence_items.source_quote: Furthermore, diminished pupillary reflex to light with preserved constriction during convergence, described as an Argyll-Robertson pupil as well as an almost complete loss of vision were found.

The diagnosis of syphilis was further confirmed by positive T. pallidum haemagglutination assay and serological activity with a rapid plasma reagin (RPR) of 1:8. A CSF study revealed pleocytosis with 93 cells/microL, predominantly mononuclear, elevated protein, albumin and lactate as well as an intrathecal synthesis of IgG-directed against T. pallidum (table 1).
evidence_items.test_name: TPHA, RPR, and CSF T. pallidum IgG

rationale: Adult male presenting with gait ataxia, bilateral optic atrophy, and classic Argyll-Robertson pupils. Confirmed tabes dorsalis (neurosyphilis) with positive TPHA, RPR 1:8, CSF pleocytosis (93 cells/uL), and intrathecal anti-T. pallidum IgG synthesis (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 23-year-old male with HIV, PML, and concurrent syphilis/neurosyphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: serum syphilis-specific antibodies were positive (treponema pallidum particle agglutination+ [TPPA+], rapid plasma reagin [RPR] 1:32+).
The patient was initially treated with ceftriaxone for syphilis and acyclovir for antiviral therapy, with slight improvement.

step10_contradiction_notes: CSF RPR was negative and CSF TPPA was weakly positive (+-), with PML (JC virus) explaining the progressive brain lesions; however, active high-titer systemic syphilis is confirmed by serum RPR 1:32+ and TPPA+ with prior generalized rash and Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction.
rationale: 23-year-old male with HIV and PML who had concurrent active syphilis: serum TPPA+ and high-titer RPR 1:32+ (E2) with prior generalized rash, old pigmented skin patches, and Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction during ceftriaxone therapy. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 30-year-old HIV-positive man with syphilitic uveitis/retinitis

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological workup revealed a reactive rapid plasma reagin (RPR) test (1:32), and in the context of the known HIV status, the patient was tested for Treponema pallidum hemagglutinin assay, which was found to be positive. The patient was diagnosed with syphilitic uveitis
RPR titers showed a downward trend (1:8) at 2 months, confirming a therapeutic response.

step10_contradiction_notes: Subsequent intermediate uveitis 2 months later was immune-mediated rather than infectious reactivation (RPR continued declining to 1:4); initial episode was active syphilitic retinitis/uveitis.
rationale: 30-year-old HIV-positive man presenting with syphilitic granulomatous uveitis and retinitis, high-titer RPR (1:32) and positive TPHA (E2), with RPR declining 4-fold to 1:8 at 2 months after penicillin/ceftriaxone/doxycycline. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 59-year-old male undergoing preoperative evaluation for urological surgery

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic evaluation confirmed active syphilitic infection, with VDRL 1:32, TPHA positive, and negative HIV screening.

Histopathologic examination demonstrated advanced atherosclerotic changes with dystrophic calcification, along with inflammatory infiltrates affecting the vasa vasorum, consistent with syphilitic aortitis.
VDRL titers decreased from 1:32 to 1:8, indicating appropriate serologic response.

rationale: A 59-year-old male with a giant aortic arch and ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm (114 x 94 x 93 mm), reactive VDRL (1:32) and TPHA, histopathologic inflammatory infiltrates of the vasa vasorum consistent with syphilitic aortitis, and a 4-fold VDRL titer drop to 1:8 two months after benzathine penicillin G therapy. Late tertiary cardiovascular syphilis is confirmed (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 2-month-old male infant with transplacentally acquired secondary/congenital syphilis (mother also TPPA+ and RPR 1:16)

evidence_items.source_quote: The results confirmed the diagnosis of secondary syphilis, indicating that the infection had been transmitted from the mother during pregnancy. TPPA assay was positive, and the rapid plasma reagin titre was 1:64.

Extensive long-strip hyperplasia was seen in both femurs, tibia and fibula, the early calcification zone was widened and the density was increased, and bone destruction was seen in both tibia and proximal medial side (Wimberger sign).

rationale: A 2-month-old male infant presenting with diffuse rash, periostitis, and Wimberger sign on lower extremity radiographs. TPPA was positive and RPR titer was 1:64 (4-fold higher than maternal RPR of 1:16), confirming congenital/secondary syphilis (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 32-year-old male with secondary syphilis sparing palms and soles, with pulmonary involvement

evidence_items.source_quote: A skin pathology reported spirochetes between the inflammatory cells observed in the dermis, using the Treponema pallidum antibody immunohistochemical (IHC) stain (Figures 2B and 2C).

Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) was slightly positive with "one dilution," and Chemiluminescence Immunoassay (CLIA) for syphilis was highly positive. Prozone phenomenon was suspected and a new diluted VDRL reported reactivity of >1:128 dilutions.

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial VDRL was only slightly positive due to prozone phenomenon; resolved with dilution (>1:128) and skin IHC.
rationale: A 32-year-old male with secondary syphilis confirmed by Treponema pallidum immunohistochemical (IHC) staining demonstrating spirochetes in skin biopsy (E1), alongside CLIA positivity and diluted VDRL >1:128.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 25-year-old male with secondary syphilis (condyloma lata of umbilicus, axilla, perianal, scrotum) and HIV coinfection

evidence_items.source_quote: Rapid plasma reagin test - 1:64 titer and T. pallidum hemagglutination assay - 1.564 tests were performed and were found to be highly positive.
Bilateral palms and soles showed hyperpigmented plaques with peripheral collarette of scales.

rationale: A 25-year-old male presenting with condyloma lata (umbilicus, axilla, perianal, scrotum) and palmar/plantar hyperpigmented plaques with peripheral collarette of scales, RPR titer 1:64 (>=1:16), and highly positive TPHA, responding to benzathine penicillin G (with Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction). Secondary syphilis is confirmed (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 67-year-old male with simultaneous myasthenia gravis and neurosyphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: Given the positive VDRL on CSF, elevated CSF protein, and lymphocytic pleocytosis, the patient was diagnosed with neurosyphilis; his neurological symptoms were attributed to early symptomatic neurosyphilis.
The patient's initial labs revealed increased inflammatory markers and positive rapid plasma reagin (RPR), which, in conjunction with the rash, were indicative of syphilis.

rationale: A 67-year-old male presenting with leg rash, positive serum RPR, and reactive CSF-VDRL with CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis and elevated CSF protein, confirming neurosyphilis (E1) alongside newly diagnosed myasthenia gravis.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 30-year-old male with neurosyphilis and otosyphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: The further CSF analysis showed a positive TPPA, a positive TRUST with a titre of 1:2, and the other concerned results like nucleated cell count, protein level and pandy test were all within the normal reference range.
there were positive reactions of Treponema Pallidum Particle Agglutination Test (TPPA), and Toluidine Red Unheated Serum Test(TRUST) with a titre of 1:1.

rationale: A 30-year-old male with progressive bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and bilateral cochlear enhancement on MRI, positive serum TPPA and TRUST (1:1), and reactive CSF TPPA and CSF TRUST (1:2), with complete audiological recovery and CSF TRUST seroreversion after ceftriaxone and benzathine penicillin. Confirmed neuro- and otosyphilis (E1).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 43-year-old female (Case 1 of series) with non-HIV ocular syphilis (bilateral panuveitis)

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood tests showed positive VDRL (1:16) with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate; whereas HIV and Mantoux tests were negative. The patient was treated with intravenous (IV) penicillin G at a dosage of 18-24 million units per day (administered as 3-4 million units every 4 h) for 2 weeks, along with oral corticosteroids (initial dose of 1 mg/kg/day) tapered over 3 months.
evidence_items.test_name: VDRL serology and IV penicillin G response

rationale: A 43-year-old immunocompetent female with bilateral panuveitis and choroiditis patches, positive VDRL (1:16) (confirmed by TPHA/FTA-ABS per series protocol in abstract), and visual recovery following 2 weeks of IV penicillin G. Ocular syphilis is confirmed (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 49-year-old female (Case 2 of series) with non-HIV ocular syphilis (neuroretinitis)

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood tests showed positive VDRL (1:32) and FTA-ABS.

rationale: A 49-year-old immunocompetent female with neuroretinitis, high-titer VDRL (1:32), and positive confirmatory FTA-ABS, improving with IV penicillin G for 14 days. Ocular syphilis is confirmed (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 24-year-old male (Case 3 of series) with non-HIV ocular syphilis (panuveitis/chorioretinitis)

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood tests indicated positivity for VDRL (1:64) and Treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay.

rationale: A 24-year-old immunocompetent male with recurrent uveitis, vitritis, and chorioretinal lesions, high-titer VDRL (1:64), and positive TPHA, improving with IV penicillin G for 2 weeks. Ocular syphilis is confirmed (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 38-year-old male (Case 4 of series) with non-HIV ocular syphilis (occlusive vasculitis and retinal detachment)

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood investigations revealed positivity for VDRL (1:64) and treponemal pallidum hemagglutinin assay (TPHA).

rationale: A 38-year-old immunocompetent male with occlusive retinal vasculitis, vitritis, and retinal detachment, high-titer VDRL (1:64), and positive TPHA, treated with IV penicillin G and procaine penicillin. Ocular syphilis is confirmed (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 54-year-old male (Case 5 of series) with non-HIV ocular syphilis (granulomatous anterior uveitis and choroiditis)

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood tests were positive for TPHA, and a 5TU Mantoux test showed an induration of 8 mm.

rationale: A 54-year-old immunocompetent male with granulomatous anterior uveitis, active choroiditis, and vascular sheathing, positive TPHA (with VDRL testing noted in series methods), tuberculosis ruled out by negative QuantiFERON, and visual improvement after 2 weeks of IV penicillin G. Ocular syphilis is supported (E2, medium confidence as VDRL titer is not stated in Case 5's individual narrative).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 46-year-old male with tertiary syphilis presenting as a penile gumma

evidence_items.source_quote: Given the benign pathology, further spirochete-specific immunohistochemical staining was performed and was positive for organisms morphologically compatible with T. pallidum (Fig. 3).
He had two nontreponemal tests (RPR) that were both nonreactive.

step10_contradiction_notes: Two RPR tests were nonreactive, but spirochete-specific T. pallidum IHC on penile biopsy was positive.
rationale: A 46-year-old male presenting with a verrucous penile gumma. Although two RPR tests were nonreactive, spirochete-specific immunohistochemical staining of the penile mass biopsy was positive for Treponema pallidum (E1 confirmatory histopathologic evidence).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 28-year-old male with secondary syphilis presenting with oral commissure mucous patches and pubic ulcer

evidence_items.source_quote: However, serological tests showed positive non-treponemal (TRUST titer 1:8) and TPPA assay, confirming the diagnosis of secondary syphilis.

Dermatological Examination at our clinic revealed an infiltrative erythematous plaque on the mons pubis with a central 2 cm ulcerated erosion, accompanied by the presence of mucous patches in the left labial commissure region, with a yellowish pseudomembrane (Figure 1).
After 3 months of treatment, the TRUST titer in the blood of the patient decreased to 1:1, and the patient is currently undergoing regular follow-up.

rationale: A 28-year-old male with mucous patches in the left labial commissure and an ulcerated erythematous plaque on the mons pubis, positive TRUST (1:8) and TPPA, and 8-fold TRUST titer decline (to 1:1) after benzathine penicillin G therapy. Secondary syphilis is confirmed (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 40-year-old male with HIV, malignant syphilis, and otosyphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory examination showed a reactive TPHA with s/co ratio of 25.94 using chemiluminescent immunoassay and VDRL test with a titer of 1:64. Therefore, the diagnosis of secondary syphilis manifesting as malignant syphilis was established.
Pure tone audiometry showed mild bilateral SNHL of 35.2 dB on the right side and 35 dB on the left side (Figure 2). This abnormal audiometry with a reactive serological test shows otosyphilis.

rationale: A 40-year-old HIV-positive male presenting with disseminated ulceronodular skin lesions (malignant secondary syphilis) with palmoplantar involvement and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (otosyphilis), high-titer VDRL (1:64), and reactive TPHA (s/co 25.94), achieving complete clinical recovery and VDRL seroconversion after IM ceftriaxone. Confirmed secondary/malignant syphilis and otosyphilis (E2).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 26-year-old male with secondary syphilitic alopecia

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological testing confirmed syphilis infection with an RPR titer of 1:32 and positive TPPA.
Copper-red maculopapular lesions were observed on both palms (Figure 2), while the soles and trunk were unaffected.
T. pallidum IHC was negative.

step10_contradiction_notes: T. pallidum IHC on penile biopsy was negative, but secondary syphilis was confirmed by RPR 1:32, positive TPPA, palmar copper-red maculopapules, moth-eaten alopecia, and lymphoplasmacytic plasma-cell infiltrate.
rationale: A 26-year-old male presenting with moth-eaten occipital alopecia, copper-red palmar maculopapular lesions, and a penile frenulum papule, with high-titer RPR (1:32) and positive TPPA. Secondary syphilis is confirmed (E2).
